# Scalar context around a class/interface intersection argument

A non-first method formal has a complete class and interface intersection.
Primitive arguments on both sides include long and double words. An inherited
virtual call preserves the original nominal value witness and all scalar bits.
Source and SDK provider layouts compile every recovered unit and compare all
original definition, Code, access, Signature, Exceptions and parameter facts.

Four frozen calling routes and a separately compiled future override exercise
128 fresh JVM cases twice. They observe null receivers and values, raw NaN and
signed-zero bits, callback replacement of caller fields, partial effects and
checked/runtime/Error identity. Wrong programs must fail independently. A
Code-preserving interface change qualifies the original late provider failure
and must be rejected by the call-site witness proof; Signature controls retain
all original method bodies and runtime descriptors.
